records.name: Avi Resort & Casino
evidence: NIGC gaming-tribe materials identify Avi Casino in Nevada under the Fort Mojave Indian Tribe.
Avi's current first-party site is active in September 2026 with current casino promotions, lodging, dining and entertainment.
Current first-party contact page confirms 10000 Aha Macav Parkway, Laughlin, Nevada 89029.

records.name: Moapa Paiute Travel Plaza
records.address: I-15 Exit 75, Valley of Fire, Moapa, NV 89025
evidence: Nevada Department of Native American Affairs lists Moapa Paiute Travel Plaza as a current tribal business.
NIGC historical compliance material identifies the Moapa Paiute Travel Plaza as a tribal gaming operation.
Current 2026 tribal-gaming directory material describes the property as a Class II/III Nevada casino with roughly 100 gaming machines.
records.scopeNote: Although travel-plaza-led, the property contains a distinct casino operation and is therefore treated as a physical tribal gaming destination rather than a generic retail slot route.

records.name: Wa She Shu Casino
records.tribe: Washoe Tribe of Nevada and California
evidence: NIGC gaming-tribe material identifies Wa She Shu Center/Casino under the Washoe Tribe.
A March 2026 tribal-gaming directory still lists Wa She Shu Casino as a Nevada tribal casino.
Current travel/review surfaces report the casino permanently closed, with multiple sources describing closure in 2023.
records.reason: Current-operation evidence is contradictory. Do not activate until a current first-party tribal/operator or authoritative regulator source confirms reopening/current gaming operation.

records.name: Palms Casino Resort
records.owner: Yuhaaviatam of San Manuel Nation / San Manuel Gaming and Hospitality Authority
records.reason: Palms is already represented in Nevada's commercial/off-Strip candidate universe. Tribal ownership does not create a second physical destination record.

notes: The tribal cross-check exists to catch physical gaming destinations that can fall outside Nevada's ordinary state nonrestricted roster logic.
Avi and Moapa should be carried into final Nevada reconciliation even if they are not represented identically to state-regulated nonrestricted casino locations.
Wa She Shu remains deliberately unresolved rather than being promoted from stale directory evidence or excluded solely from third-party closure reports.
